title: Earlier BATS water types need at least 17.5 percent reassigned weight to fit both epoch means without added oxygen use
abstract: We test how much source weights must change to explain the BATS oxygen loss without extra oxygen use. We fit the 1989-1998 and 2016-2025 five-property means with two normalized mixtures of earlier individual bottles. We minimize half the sum of absolute weight changes. For a local 1989-2009 source library on density 26.2-26.8, an exact no-added-use fit needs at least 17.46 percent reassigned weight. Temperature and salinity alone need 7.32 percent. Adding oxygen raises the bound to 16.42 percent; nitrate and phosphate raise it to 17.46 percent. A wider density library gives 16.80 percent. Sources limited to 1989-1998 give 29.94 percent in the main density range. At 10 micromol/kg of added oxygen use, the main bound falls to 8.59 percent. Diagnostic property error allowances lower the no-added-use bound to 13.58 percent. A separate shared-mass optimization checks the result. The bounds are sharp for the stated finite libraries. They are not transport estimates or proof that mixing caused the oxygen loss. Missing sources, sampling, fixed reaction ratios and absent dynamic constraints limit inference. Code, aggregate data, provenance and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Minimum change of normalized source weights needed to fit both BATS epoch means. Extra oxygen use and the allowed density range change the bounds.
